analysis.investment_thesis: Nazara is a serial acquirer in gaming — a sector I have no expertise in and no affinity for — trading at 133x earnings despite a 9-year net profit CAGR of -2.7% and ROE of just 2.9%. Revenue growth funded by equity dilution with near-zero returns on capital is not a business I will ever own.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.06 — clean balance sheet, no meaningful leverage
Revenue growing at 25.5% CAGR (2016-2025), demonstrating market presence in digital gaming
High gross margin of 71% shows the underlying content/IP has value
key_risks: Promoter holding only 35.45% — far below my 55% minimum, signals weak owner-operator alignment
Net profit declined from ₹65 Cr (2016) to ₹51 Cr (2025) over 9 years despite 8x revenue growth — wealth is being destroyed
Acquisition machine burning cash (Investing CF: -1,139 Cr in 2025) funded by perpetual equity dilution — shareholders bear all the risk
red_flags: P/E of 133.6x and EV/EBITDA of 100.8x — among the most expensive stocks I have ever seen relative to actual earnings quality
ROE of 2.9% and ROCE of 2.5% — I would earn more in a fixed deposit; this destroys capital
Operating margin of only 1.98% on ₹1,624 Cr revenue — nearly all gross profit evaporates into costs
Other Income (₹80 Cr) is 70% of operating income (₹115 Cr) — reported profits are not from operations
FCF turned negative in 2025 (-₹82 Cr) as capex surged to ₹148 Cr; no dividends ever paid
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my perspective, Nazara fails nearly every test I apply before investing a single rupee. ROE of 2.9% is not a business — it is capital in slow decay. Nine years of 25% revenue growth with net profits actually shrinking (₹65 Cr → ₹51 Cr, CAGR of -2.7%) tells me management is skilled at buying companies but incapable of generating returns on the capital deployed. The entire ₹2,894 Cr equity base expansion since 2020 has been funded by shareholders, and those shareholders have received virtually nothing back — no dividends, no meaningful earnings, and negative free cash flow in the latest year.

The valuation is disconnected from reality in a way that makes me deeply uncomfortable. At 133x P/E and 100x EV/EBITDA, the market is pricing perfection for a decade into a sector (gaming, esports, edtech) that I consider structurally difficult — low switching costs, constant content refresh cycles, fierce global competition, and a technology disruption risk I cannot underwrite. Promoter holding at 35.45% is a further disqualifier for me; I want founders with the majority of their net worth on the line alongside me. I would not hold this stock at any price near current levels.
